editorNote: A release-heavy Saturday: Moonshot's open-weight promise, an unsubstantiated iPhone claim, and tooling and standards details worth reading closely. Benchmarks and claims are the publishers' own.

stories.headline: Moonshot ships Kimi K3.1 Pro, with open weights promised by Nov. 4
stories.summary: Moonshot's K3.1 Pro is a post-trained Kimi K3 with a 1M-token context, plus a Highspeed variant it says runs 2-3x faster. It reports 65.7% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 against 66.4% for Claude Opus 5.5, and an 8.3% claim-level hallucination rate against K3's 23.4%.
stories.whyItMatters: All benchmarks are Moonshot's own, and the weights are a promise until Nov. 4; it is available now via API and apps.

sourceLinks.title: Kimi K3.1 Pro and K3.1 Pro Highspeed - Kimi

stories.headline: Calif says it hacked the iPhone, showing demos at Hexacon
stories.summary: A short Oct. 16 post says the team 'hacked what we'd set out to hack: the iPhone', with demo captions mentioning a Signal 1-click and iMessage. It names no iOS version or technique and says everything 'will be released in due time'.
stories.whyItMatters: Claim without details so far; nothing is verifiable until the write-up lands, and the post does not say whether Apple was notified.

sourceLinks.title: Today, we hacked what we'd set out to hack: the iPhone - Calif

stories.headline: Astral previews 'uv check', wiring the ty type checker into uv
stories.summary: The experimental integration adds a uv check command that builds the environment and runs ty, with --package, --all-packages and --script options, and PEP 723 script support. It needs uv 0.12.3+ and ty 0.0.76+; Ruff is planned next.
stories.whyItMatters: Type checking now uses the lockfile's pinned ty version, so developers and CI run the same checker.

sourceLinks.title: Bringing uv and ty together - Astral

stories.headline: Block's Dessa is a full-duplex conversation model trained only on speech
stories.summary: Block's research lab says Dessa learned from human conversation audio alone, with no text or pretrained models, using one NVIDIA GB200 NVL72. It lists no benchmarks or parameter count; access is a waitlist plus an application for AI safety researchers.
stories.whyItMatters: 'World's first' is the authors' claim, supported only by demo recordings; nothing is publicly downloadable yet.

stories.headline: EFF urges Canadians to oppose Bill C-22 as it reaches the Senate
stories.summary: EFF says the Lawful Access Act, passed by the House, would let the Public Safety Minister order backdoors short of 'systemic insecurity', require up to a year of metadata retention, and could widen data sharing with foreign police. The CCLA and Citizen Lab want Part 2 withdrawn.
stories.whyItMatters: The bill now sits in the Senate; the EFF post gives no deadline.

sourceLinks.title: Canadians Are Running Out of Time to Oppose Dangerous C-22 Surveillance Bill - EFF

stories.headline: UUIDv7's timestamps are less trustworthy than advertised, one author argues
stories.summary: The post says only uniqueness is guaranteed: Python's uuid.uuid7() can run ahead of the clock without bound after a backward clock step (over an hour in the author's test), and ordering can break on restarts. It advises asking each implementation what it guarantees.
stories.whyItMatters: Code treating UUIDv7 as a creation time or strict sort key is relying on behaviour the RFC leaves to implementations.

sourceLinks.title: UUIDv7: Timestamps aren't time-ordered and other oddities - alexsci.com
